opening.argument: The video presents Fandango as a practical movie-ticket application, beginning with the explanation that it is “a movie app for buying movie tickets” used to purchase tickets. It then demonstrates ordinary operational features: checking nearby theater showtimes, reserving seats, proceeding through payment, and viewing ticket prices. The transaction is transparently framed as a movie purchase, including the stated service fee, rather than as an offer of unusual returns, guaranteed rewards, or financial gain. The gift-card feature is likewise presented as a conventional Fandango product that can be bought for someone else. Although the description includes an external Amazon gift-card giveaway link, the supplied evidence does not establish deceptive entry conditions, credential collection, or victim loss. The available material therefore supports an educational technology demonstration and review, with no basis to extend the evidence beyond those limits.
